summary.summary: PARTIAL - the FKG lattice condition for the occupation marginal mu(A) = z^|A| Z_A of the law with vacancies is PROVED for the two-valued menu, modulo Griffiths' second inequality: the site count is modular and the edge set supermodular with E(A n B) = E(A) n E(B) and E(A) u E(B) contained in E(A u B) (both verified over all ordered pairs of subsets of a ring of 6 and a 3x3 torus), so the coupling vectors satisfy J(A n B) = J(A) ^ J(B) and J(A u B) >= J(A) v J(B); since log Z is increasing and supermodular in the couplings - the latter being GKS-II, checked here on every ordered pair of edges of three small graphs - log mu is supermodular, which upgrades attempt a4's four exhaustive instance checks to a theorem for every graph, every z > 0 and every beta >= 0; but GKS-II is an Ising theorem and is not available for O(3) spins, so for the SPHERE menu that this unit is actually about, rho_2 >= rho^2 still rests on a4's numerics

review: Both priors are mine, so I took a4's section 4 item 1 - prove the lattice condition it could only check. It factors into three pieces: modularity of the site count, supermodularity of the edge set with E(AnB) = E(A) n E(B) exactly, and supermodularity of log Z in the couplings. Only the third has content and it is exactly Griffiths' second inequality, which I mark ASSUMED and verify on every edge pair of three small graphs. That proves a4's hypothesis for the two-valued menu at every graph, fugacity and coupling. The point I want on the record is where it fails: GKS-II is an Ising theorem and is not available for vector spins, so the SPHERE menu this unit is actually about is not covered by the proof - pieces one and two are menu-independent, the physics step is not. I then checked how far past Ising the step survives and found non-negative covariances at q = 2,3,4,6, so there is no small-q counterexample and the sphere case looks true-but-unproved rather than doubtful. I replaced a tautological check of my own before shipping. This is my third attempt on this problem in one session and a shared error would propagate through all three; the chain wants an outside referee.
